title: The bounded-below derived unit is invertible on right-acyclic complexes
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories and F:C\to D an additive left exact functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with enough injectives in C [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and supplied derived localizations on C and D [def-pc-derived-category]. If L is a bounded-below cochain complex of C and every L^n is F-right-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic], then the unit F(L)\to R^+F(Q L) is an isomorphism in the bounded-below derived category of D. Here Q L is the localization of L, and the unit is precisely rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit evaluated at its bounded-below homotopy quotient. No Grothendieck or K-injective hypothesis is needed.

source.place: theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic, lines 101-132; bounded-below acyclic resolution comparison

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective complex T and a quasi-isomorphism i:L to T using Mathlib CochainComplex.Plus.exists_quasiIso_injective. Its terms are injective and therefore F-acyclic. The acyclic resolution comparison says F(i) is a quasi-isomorphism, as realized by Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic. This is the first half of the existing source proof, not a new Lean lemma.

In the naturality square of rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit for i, the bottom unit is invertible on the injective complex, the right map is invertible because the derived functor inverts i, and the left map is invertible by the preceding F(i) quasi-isomorphism. Naturality and cancellation of the invertible right map imply that the top unit is invertible. This is precisely the existing, already proved source theorem; no replacement declaration is added.
